head.name: @fzlt/core/steer
head.lead: How things move toward, away from and around a point, as DOM-free steering on typed arrays. Every mover has a position (x, y), a heading (a, radians) that turns at most turn rad/s, and moves speed × scale px/s along it. Behaviours: - seek: drive at a point, stop inside stop; - flee: drive straight away from a point until far; - arrive: seek with an arrival band: full pace far off, slower inside slow, stop inside near; arriveGoal is the same toward the goal the game wrote in gx[i], gy[i] (a target that moves every frame: no double crosses a call, so nothing is boxed); - wander: pick a random goal in area every every + random × jitter s and seek it; - patrol: seek waypoints in turn, looping. Each writes the distance moved this call to moved[i] (0 when standing). The heading turn and the per-axis wall check (blocked, so a mover slides along walls) are DOM Battlefield Blitz's drive, and the defaults are its tank numbers, so a port keeps its feel. Nothing allocates: call them from a step, one mover at a time. Pass engine.random as random so seeded runs replay: the heading's trig is @fzlt/core/math's, so a replay gives the same bits in every browser (in Node, the builtins' bits: the moves are Blitz's to the bit). Options are checked at setup: a bad number throws a RangeError with its name instead of turning into NaN mid-game.

items.doc: Math.hypot of two numbers, without the builtin call: V8 boxes Math.hypot's arguments, a heap number per call in a hot loop. Same steps as V8's own (Infinity wins over NaN, scale by the larger, sum, sqrt), so it returns the same bits (tested against Math.hypot).
